title: Presolana rehearsal: 1600m D+, descent capped 1000m, the 80 g/h duration test
terrain: Presolana, ONE sustained climb ~1600m D+, descent hard-capped 1000m, fixed line

steps.target: Z2-Z3 single sustained climb ~1600m D+, 151-160 bpm
Z1-Z2 descent, capped 1000m, poles, cadence 175+, 99-144 bpm

coachNotes:
EXECUTION: one climb and out, ~4h15 total. 1600m D+, descent hard-capped at 1000m. Fixed line, fixed endpoint, load the GPX, no summit out-and-backs. Descend with poles, short stride, cadence 175+. If the route offers more descent than 1000m, take the lift or the road.
GYM: none.
FUEL, THE RANKED OBJECTIVE: 80 g/h from minute 30 to the finish. 1 Isocarb C2:1 Pro sachet-equivalent per 500ml, one bottle per hour, plus 1 Carbo Gel at hour 2 and hour 4. DRINK ON THE CLOCK: 125ml every 15min, not to thirst. That single instruction is the whole test.
STOP RULE: no symptoms during, after, or next day. If holding the intake means cutting the route, cut the route. 1600m at 40 g/h is a wasted last chance.
WHY IT IS RESTORED: cut to 900m on 24 Aug after the knee signal, held there on 26 Aug pending evidence outside the shockwave analgesic window, restored now on a clean 30 Aug long run and a clean Monday morning. Descent is the reason for the middle option rather than the full 1200m: Pirin finishes with a continuous 1250m descent onto seven-hour legs and arriving with a 600m maximum in the previous three weeks is genuinely under-prepared, but this is the last day a descent error can still be paid for.
WHY THE DRINKING RULE: on 30 Aug the gut took 96 g/h without complaint, so carbohydrate tolerance is not the constraint. Drinking volume is. He took 404 ml/h and felt fine, but this system needs 500 ml/h to deliver its 60g from the bottle - at 400 ml/h the total silently lands near 68 g/h instead of 80, with nothing that feels wrong.
